title: Hybrid header anchors and intelligent pagination for large grid UX
creator: Marco Ruiz
description: Introduce a hybrid interaction pattern for very large virtualized tables that combines header anchor affordances with intelligent, progressive pagination. Goal is to preserve keyboard/aria navigation and smooth column-resize/sort/filter interactions while avoiding expensive full-viewport virtualization calculations for wide, deep datasets. This ticket covers visual spec, interaction model, accessibility mapping, and handoff artifacts for engineering implementation.
acceptance_criteria: Design spec describes header anchor states (focused, pinned, hover) and their keyboard affordances
Pagination behavior documented for progressive loads (anchor-based incremental pages and seamless jump-to-row) with performance and UX rationale
Column-resize interaction prototypes show stable header anchors during fast resizes and when virtualized rows are reflowed
Sorting and filtering flows demonstrate no loss of focus or context when results change size, with clear fallback for large result sets
Accessibility matrix maps to ARIA roles, live region announcements for pagination actions, and keyboard-only workflows validated
Design handoff includes annotated Figma screens + component token variants for 3 density profiles (compact, standard, relaxed) and a small set of micro-interaction specs (hover, active, collapse)
Two engineering-feasible implementation approaches outlined: (A) sticky header anchors + windowed virtualization, (B) paginated virtualization with focus-preserving anchors — tradeoffs documented
design_notes: Problem: users lose orientation when virtualization drops rows during fast resize or jump-to actions; keyboard focus can be lost when list reflows

Proposal: keep header-level anchor affordances (tiny anchor icons + drag handles) that act as persistent focus anchor points; anchors are semantic controls that map to keyboard shortcuts (A to anchor menu, J/K to jump pages)

Pagination: use progressive pages that load contiguous ranges of rows (eg. 200 rows) while allowing a seamless scroll+fetch experience; present soft page boundaries visually only when user requests jump-to or large scroll
Density: tokens for padding, touch target, and hit areas will have three named variants; resizing and collapse behavior must reuse tokens rather than bespoke values
Column resizing: when a user starts a drag, freeze virtualization for the header zone and render a 1-2 row buffer to prevent header-heartbeat from shifting anchor positions

Sorting/filtering: use ephemeral banners to indicate active query transforms and provide a quick-undo affordance; preserve anchor focus after result mutation by mapping old row id -> new index if present
decisions: Chosen: hybrid approach leaning toward sticky header anchors + minimal windowed virtualization as default for performance and simpler keyboard preservation
Fallback: paginated virtualization will be offered as a configuration when memory constraints require strict bounding of the render window
Density tokens: adopt existing spacing scale (ds-space-2, ds-space-3, ds-space-4) and expose component-level token aliases (table.padding.compact/standard/relaxed)
Accessibility: announce page changes via aria-live polite and keep focus on anchor control rather than shifting to content to avoid disorientation
tradeoffs: Continuity vs performance: keeping more buffer rows improves focus stability but increases render cost on low-end devices
Complexity vs flexibility: header anchors add conceptual overhead for users but provide a stable anchor point for keyboard users and when results mutate
Engineering effort vs UX polish: animated smooth jumps are nicer but add complexity and potential for jank — plan: MVP uses instant jumps with a lightweight fade-in
